title: 2026-03-21-poc-stability-load-burst-root-cause-review
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on yesterday's burst of 5xx/timeouts during peak batch ingestion. We walked through telemetry, hypothesized causes (queue saturation + retry amplification + an aggressive client-side retry policy), discussed short-term mitigations (rate-limit floors, backoff jitter, circuit breaker), and agreed on tests and artifacts to share. Next steps: synthetic replay, upload debug bundle, short config tweak on rate limits + reduce default retries, and schedule a 2-hour runbook/drill before EOW.
next_steps: Customer to upload full debug bundle + sample request IDs by 2026-03-23
Redwood SE to provision synthetic replay harness and run controlled burst by 2026-03-24
AE to share pricing/commit options for Dedicated in case of traffic >95th pct by 2026-03-27
Schedule 2-hour incident-drill with SRE + Redwood SE for 2026-03-26
action_items: Jenna Park (SRE): export request/response traces and send redwood-debug-bundle.zip to maya@redwood.com; due 2026-03-23
Carlos Ortega (SE): stand up synthetic replay (50-200 rps burst profile) and share test harness link; due 2026-03-24
Maya Lin (AE): send short pricing note for dedicated pool options and pilot overage triggers; due 2026-03-27
Tom Alvarez (ML Eng): try reduced client-side retries (2 -> 1) in canary and report 24h error rate; due 2026-03-24
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jenna (Clerico SRE), Tom (Clerico ML Eng), Rita (Product), Samir (Infra)

Summary: quick recap at start—yesterday afternoon there was a 15-minute window of elevated 5xx and timeouts during a customer ingestion peak. We'll go through logs, hypothesize root cause, and align on mitigations and tests.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we'll keep this tight — 42 minutes on the calendar. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Jenna (Clerico): Jenna here. We had some follow-ups from the incident, a couple of escalations.
[00:17] Tom (Clerico): Tom — ready with logs.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood): Carlos here, I pulled the partial traces you shared last night.
[00:26] Maya: Cool, agenda — telemetry review, root-cause hypotheses, short-term mitigations, and then assign actions.
[00:32] (short cross-talk)
[00:36] [00:36] Priya (Redwood CSM): One note — customer success getting pinged on SLA questions, so let's call out any window where they'll need a statement.

[02:03] Jenna: To summarize the incident: at ~14:08 UTC we saw a spike from the ingestion pipeline, roughly 180 rps sustained for 12 minutes, then intermittent retries from the client stack. Our key symptom is an increasing 502/5xx rate and a few long tail timeouts ~7-12s.
[02:28] Tom: I'll drop the request IDs in chat after the call. The ingress is a kaf ka consumer that fans out into batches to the Redwood API.
[02:41] Maya: Noted — kaf ka -> batch -> Redwood. Two quick clarifying q's: did you have prefix caching or KV cache enabled for this route?
[02:55] Tom: We turned on KV caching for prompt prefixes, but it's on the default eviction.
[03:05] Carlos: Ok. Initial observation from the traces — many requests succeeded quickly but a subset queued up behind long-running generation calls. We see queue length climb in the worker pool, and when queue > threshold we started returning 502s from the proxy layer.
[03:29] Samir: We also saw increased connection churn at the client side — they retried aggressively (no jitter) and that looks like it amplified the load.
[03:44] Rita: To be clear, this is P0 for product because users saw degraded latency.

[04:20] Maya: I'm going to sketch a working hypothesis: high incoming burst + some heavy long-context requests -> worker queue saturation -> proxy-level 502s -> client retries without exponential backoff -> retry amplification -> longer queues -> 5xx tail. Agree/ disagree?
[04:45] Tom: Sounds right. One nuance — about 10% of the requests were to the larger 13B model with long max tokens. Those took 2-3x CPU/GPU time compared to the 7B model.
[05:02] Carlos: That's a helpful data point. Model heterogeneity + lack of routing could create hot slots. Also the KV cache miss rate was high for those 13B requests since prefixes varied.

[06:10] Jenna: We also noticed telemetry gaps — trace sampling at 5% meant we missed some sequences and can't tie retries to exact triggered errors in all cases.
[06:28] Carlos: Right. We recommend bumping trace sampling to 25% for the pilot window — just during tests — so we can get full waterfall traces.
[06:40] Maya: Actionable mitigation for the immediate term: (1) apply client-side change to reduce retries and add jitter, (2) server-side put a rate-limit floor and a soft queue-limit with early 429 (not 502), and (3) fallback routing to smaller model for requests exceeding size threshold. Carlos, any pitfalls?
[07:05] Carlos: For (2) the proxy returns 502 once internal queue backs up — we can change that to return 429 earlier and annotate with x-retry-after header. For fallback routing, we'll need a quick canary rule that routes heavy requests to the 7B model when throughput > X. There's a tradeoff: quality vs latency/cost.
[07:31] Tom: For the canary rule — how fast can Redwood flip it? We need 5-10 minute turnarounds.
[07:38] Carlos: We can roll that config in < 15 minutes during low risk windows; but we'll test in the staging canary first.

[08:10] (interruption)
[08:22] Samir: Another detail — we're running the client retry at 4 tries with no jitter and a 1s base; that's aggressive.
[08:31] Maya: If you drop it to 1 retry with randomized jitter between 200-1200ms, that should cut amplification significantly.
[08:40] Tom: We'll try that immediately for the canary route.

[09:05] Jenna: On the server side we saw a pattern where certain worker nodes had disproportionately high GPU memory churn. Could that be due to long context KV operations?
[09:18] Carlos: Possibly. Our runtime keeps per-request KV buffers; if many large-context requests land on same node you'll see GC/ memory churn. We can look at more even routing or enable prefix caching at a broader granularity.
[09:36] Rita: Any quick config we can toggle to reduce memory churn?
[09:43] Carlos: Lower the per-request max length or enforce smaller max concurrent streams per worker. That will reduce peak memory temporarily.

[10:12] Maya: Let's list concrete mitigations into short-term and medium-term. Short-term (minutes-hours): reduce client retries + add jitter, move heavy requests to smaller /q canary, lower concurrent streams on busiest workers, change early responses to 429 with Retry-After. Medium-term (days): smarter routing by model cost, KV cache tuning, better trace sampling and token-level billing visibility.

[11:05] Tom: About 429 vs 502 — some of our infra interprets 429 as retryable too; will that still help?
[11:12] Carlos: We recommend 429 with Retry-After and advise client to respect Retry-After and backoff. The key is to convert hard failures to explicit backoff signals so clients don't hammer.
[11:29] Jenna: We can update the client library, but older instances may not have the updated handler. Any way to make the server side less permissive for older clients?
[11:40] Maya: We can set a configurable header and also set a short-lived feature flag on the server to send X-Redwood-RateHint so newer clients handle it gracefully. Older clients will still retry but with the reduced global rate the amplification reduces.

[12:22] (short pause)
[12:30] Carlos: I want to call out an observability gap — token-level cost attribution and per-route latency percentiles are not currently in your dashboards. We can push a quick export for the pilot.
[12:43] Samir: That would be helpful to justify dedicated pool costs.

[13:15] Maya: Ok, drilling into traces — looking at Request ID 8b4f which Tom pasted, we see a pattern: initial request to 13B model, took ~1.8s to schedule, then 9s to run; meanwhile multiple client retries came in and stacked. By the time the worker finished the first, the proxy had already started returning 502 for queued requests.
[13:45] Tom: That matches our logs. The stack currently marks high latency as transient and immediately retries. We'll change that.

[14:12] Rita: Are there any immediate costs/ billing impacts if we route heavy flows to a cheaper model?
[14:20] Maya: It's usually cheaper per-token on smaller models, but you might have quality loss. Redwood Optimize can give per-workload expected quality delta; we'll run an eval on sample prompts.

[15:02] Jenna: On the incident postmortem we want a crisp statement for internal stakeholders. Can Redwood provide a one-paragraph timeline we can paste into our internal incident doc?
[15:10] Maya: Yes we'll provide a timeline and the mitigations we applied. Priya will draft the messaging.

[16:00] (discussion about runbook)
[16:10] Carlos: We should create a short runbook: detection rule (error rate > 3% for > 3m), immediate steps (flip fallback rule, reduce client retries, invoke circuit breaker), and escalation path.
[16:26] Samir: That sounds good; can we add an automated run that runs a synthetic burst nightly at 2am for early detection?
[16:35] Carlos: We can schedule that, but might want it to run against a canary pool so it doesn't affect prod users.

[17:12] Tom: For the synthetic replay — what's a representative burst profile? 150-200 rps for 10-15 minutes?
[17:19] Carlos: Yes, and mix in 10% long-context 13B traffic to simulate worst-case. We'll also include jitter and retry behaviors.

[18:00] (noise)
[18:20] Jenna: We'll need to think about SLO implications. Product will want a threshold that triggers sales outreach.
[18:28] Maya: AE note — I'll propose a pilot SLA addendum: if sustained 95th pct latency > X then we convene a support conference and consider dedicated pool options.

[19:05] Rita: Any blockers on our side to try the short-term changes?
[19:10] Tom: We'll push a canary client release today to drop retries and add jitter.
[19:18] Jenna: We'll also compile the debug bundle and upload.

[20:06] Carlos: Two operational notes: ensure your trace correlation IDs are preserved across the Kaf ka fan-out so Redwood traces can connect end-to-end, and include worker node IDs in the logs.
[20:20] Tom: Good call, we'll add that.

[21:05] Maya: Security/compliance quick callout — does any mitigation require changes that affect data residency?
[21:12] Samir: No, these are config and routing changes within the same region.

[22:00] (short lull)
[22:12] Carlos: On the longer-term fix — intelligent routing: we'll build a small model-cost estimator that takes expected token count + model type and routes to the least-cost/ least-latency option under current load. That needs a couple of weeks to test.
[22:30] Tom: That would be great.

[23:00] (acknowledgements)
[23:10] Maya: Let's confirm owners for the items: Jenna uploads debug bundle, Carlos does synthetic harness, Tom does client canary, Maya shares pricing. Priya drafts incident blurb.

[24:05] Tom: Quick question — what about automated circuit breakers on the client side? Should we design a per-route limiter?
[24:15] Carlos: Per-route limiter is useful; it can be token-aware and use a moving window to avoid penalizing short-lived bursts. We'll prototype.

[25:20] Jenna: Timeline ask — can we get the synthetic run and initial findings by 2026-03-24?
[25:27] Carlos: Yes, that's the plan.

[26:00] Rita: Any legal/ procurement items from this? We might need an addendum if we move to dedicated racks.
[26:08] Maya: AE will follow-up if we need contract language.

[27:15] (brief side discussion about metrics)
[28:10] Maya: Ok, any final questions?
[28:20] Tom: Not from me. We'll start the client canary in the next hour.
[28:30] Jenna: I'll get the debug bundle uploaded and drop IDs in the shared slack channel.

[30:00] Priya: We'll set up the incident-drill meeting for 2026-03-26; invite will come from Priya.
[30:12] Maya: Great. Last thing — any competitor mentions? Jenna: some internal discussion compared Redwood to Anthropic on rate-limiting semantics; noted.

[31:00] (wrap)
[31:10] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the action items.
[31:15] (call ends)

Notes: Transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors in a few lines (standard firflies transcripts). Shared artifacts: link to debug bundle (to be uploaded), synthetic replay repo: https://redwood.internal/synthetic-replay/clerico-burst, pilot dashboard snapshot: https://app.redwood.com/pilot/clerico/dashboard (view-only), postmortem template: https://docs.redwood.com/pilot-postmortem-template
